A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Compact Conformal Subgraphs by the same authors. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic navigation and planted trip-planning experiments in Section 5, plus analysis of Porto taxi trajectories in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and real-data results, consolidated in Appendix G.

M1.justification: New Section 2.4 sketches procedural extensions: passing nested subgraphs into risk-controlling prediction sets and applying compression separately within difficulty categories. The core LP, threshold rounding, sampling, and fixed-context procedures remain unchanged; the min-cut procedure already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic grid-and-bypass navigation scenario, Porto airport-to-center trajectories, and planted trip-planning model. The new risk-control and conditional-coverage discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Forward Greedy and Reverse Greedy remain the navigation comparators in both synthetic and Porto experiments. The trip-planning experiment retains comparison with the planted core size, without adding competing methods.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain their preprocessing, splits, coverage metrics, and settings: 50 training and 50 held-out synthetic routes, 100/100 Porto routes, and 100/100 trip-planning samples. The grid sizes, traffic mixtures, planted probability, and core-density sweep also match.

E4.justification: The route-selection illustrations and planted-core density analysis are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or empirical case study accompanies their relocation to Appendix G.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10-run navigation comparisons and display identical error bars. There are no added or revised seed disclosures, repeated-run counts, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: All six embedded plot/image panels are identical. v1 Figures 1, 2, and 3 correspond to v2 Figures 1, 3, and 2, respectively. Numerical findings and interpretations of the plotted trends remain unchanged, including the 52-edge synthetic and 797-edge Porto illustrations.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds a randomized-threshold proof of Lagrangian integrality, previously stated with a citation, and Appendix A expands its Stage-1-failure argument. Theorem 2 reorganizes the earlier monotonicity theorem and Corollary 1; the principal approximation, hardness, validity, and sampling guarantees are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the stated contributions to general-loss risk control and category-wise conditional coverage, supported by new Section 2.4. The abstract and central claims about compact subgraphs, bicriteria approximation, and monotone conformal calibration remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds discussion of the coarseness of all-or-nothing coverage and the limitations of exact finite-sample conditional coverage. Section 4.1 explicitly explains when the bicriteria bound becomes vacuous, and the introduction qualifies the experiments as proof of concept for primarily theoretical work.

D1.justification: Experimental implementation descriptions, data preparation, hyperparameters, sampling instructions, and the under-one-minute runtime statement are retained. The expanded main-text min-cut construction was already documented in v1 Appendix D; no new code, hardware, or data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bates et al. on risk-controlling prediction sets, Vovk on conditional validity, and Chekuri et al. on densest subgraphs. It explicitly attributes the hypergraph min-cut reduction to prior work and identifies preservation through LP optimization and rounding as its contribution. Other bibliography changes largely update existing works.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: empirical Section 5 and the former traffic appendix are consolidated into Appendix G, while the min-cut construction moves from Appendix D into an expanded Section 4.2. The introduction is rewritten, Section 2.4 is added, and the proof organization is revised to emphasize the theoretical contribution.

P2.justification: The existing figures are relocated and reordered, with Porto becoming Figure 2 and trip planning Figure 3. Their panels, dimensions, axes, legends, and plotted content are unchanged. The remaining visual differences are page reflow and placement changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and self-containment through the explicit integrality proof, clearer high-coverage applicability discussion, and more precise attribution of the min-cut reduction. The theoretical organization is easier to follow while retaining all empirical evidence. The new risk-control and conditional-coverage extensions remain sketches, so the gains are limited rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
